translations.text: And again: “I was an object of reproach among men and of contempt among the people.”
“Everyone who sees me mocks me. They speak with their lips and shake their heads.”
And again: “Those who sit at the gates spoke against me, and those who drink wine sang songs about me.”
And: “Because of you I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face.” And again: “I encountered affliction and distress, and I cried out to the Lord.”
And again: “Do not be silent, God, and do not remain still. Look, your enemies have cried out, and those who hate me have raised their heads.”
As for me, I do not make an effort to do what I ought to do.
But as for these others, this is a way of death: even if regions are laid waste, they pursue their own business, namely plunder.
For often, even if the soldier does his utmost and does not win, it is clear that God is the one who raises our enemies against us because of our sins.
At other times, however, it is nothing but the negligence of those who govern, who fail to do what they ought to do.

For the matter is clear when the authorities and the soldier risk their lives for those for whom they fight, knowing that the Lord is the one who gives strength and victory. But when they do not give their attention to the work, you will find them all the more readily at the time of plundering.

What does the hunter do? He makes an effort to obtain an animal, or some animals, and places it around his nets and hunting equipment, until many gather and many come, and until they become [?] with one another in the trap.
The one who committed the sin also committed the evil deed.
